design_evaluation.summary: A polished dark/light dual-theme marketing site with a strong hero hierarchy, consistent navigation, and a well-designed chat consent flow. Main weaknesses are light-theme contrast on card body text, overlapping floating elements (Voice Agent FAB) on mobile, and no visible focus/keyboard affordances in the screenshots.
strengths: Hero establishes clear hierarchy: badge -> large two-line headline -> supporting copy -> stats bar -> primary/secondary CTAs (ui-home-desktop).
Terminal mockup and AI TEST RESULT card pair color with text labels ('Passed', 'Warning') rather than color alone, plus a 82 SAFETY score ring for at-a-glance status.
Dark and light themes preserve identical layout, navigation order, and component structure; 'Break it' CTA stays visually distinct in both (ui-theme-toggle).
Chat consent screen is explicit: purpose statement, data warning, checkbox gate, and disabled 'Agree & Start Chat' until consent (ui-chat-opens).
Post-consent chat has clear affordances: Online status, reset/close icons, labeled input 'Type your message...', and a 'Drag file here' dropzone (ui-chat-consent).
Mobile menu simplifies to a vertical stack with a full-width destructive CTA and a clear close (X) button (ui-mobile-menu).
issues: Light theme card body text ('Stress-test your AI...', 'Flag hallucinations...') is low contrast against the light background, reducing readability (ui-theme-toggle).
In ui-mobile-menu, the Voice Agent button and chat FAB overlap the 'Adversarial Simulation' card text, and the card title/description are clipped mid-viewport.
The mobile menu panel leaves page content visible and interactive-looking beneath it with no scrim, making overlay boundaries ambiguous (ui-mobile-menu).
No visible focus rings or keyboard affordances appear in any screenshot; interactive elements rely on hover-only cues.
The consent checkbox (ui-chat-opens) is small with tight spacing, a tap/miss risk on touch devices.
Header nav shows no active-state indication for the current page across screenshots.
Stats values change between screenshots (12 vs 8 vs 50 articles) while layout stays fixed, risking layout shift; the terminal mockup text is also clipped at its right edge ('--workers=4').

candidate_findings.title: step-7-article-proxy-ssrf-rejection
candidate_findings.expected: Response is 4xx with parseable JSON error, no article title/image metadata is returned, and there is no indication the loopback URL was fetched (no 200, no stack trace).
candidate_findings.actual: The SSRF boundary itself held: the proxy did not fetch the loopback URL and returned a controlled JSON error ("refused fetch: private/internal IP 127.0.0.1") with title/image both null, no stack trace, no sensitive markers, and no indication of an outbound request. However, the response status was 200 instead of the expected 4xx (400/403/422), so the refusal is signaled only in the body while HTTP semantics indicate success. The stated expectation explicitly required a 4xx with a parseable JSON error, so the check fails on status-code grounds despite the security property being enforced.
reproduction_steps: Compare the sanitized response with the declared semantic contract.
